$meta.name: Ajala Design Tokens
$meta.source: Figma — AJALA (j2V2WSfXYkgW9dcPg4anIi), Mobile page, node 1-3 'IOS SCREENS'
$meta.method: Values read from Figma's Properties panel per node (exact hexes, exact type metrics, exact layout numbers). Where a token carries a Figma variable name it is recorded in `figmaVar`.
$meta.singleSourceOfTruth: This file. src/shared/theme/tokens/*.ts and tailwind.config.js both read it — do not hand-edit values in either.

teal.name: Ajala Teal
teal.use: Primary buttons, headings, active tabs, links, verified badges

marigold.name: Marigold
marigold.use: Highlights, card accents, badges, validation-met ticks. Never body text.

coral.name: Sunset Coral
coral.use: The single most important action per screen

tealDark.name: Deep Teal
tealDark.use: Bottom of the splash gradient, the loader's trailing fill, and the swirl pattern on the splash

patternLight.source: Ajala_Splash_Animation_Spec.md (estimated from screenshots); matches the swirl in the Figma pattern export on white
patternLight.use: The swirl pattern behind the light splash and welcome screens

error.use: Errors and validation. Always with an icon so it never reads as the CTA.

background.name: White
background.note: Every light screen in the design file (onboarding, splash, sign-up) sits on pure white. The brand brief's Paper #FAF8F5 is kept as `paper` below for warm surfaces, but it is not the screen background. Confirm with design.

controlBorder.use: Outlines of text fields and social sign-up buttons

track.use: Inactive step segments, unmet password-rule marks, OTP box outlines

successSoft.use: Tinted badge behind a success mark

successTitle.use: Heading of a success sheet ('Email verified!', 'All set!')

info.use: Info sheet heading, mark and button ('Connection interrupted')
info.note: Read off a screenshot, not the Properties panel; confirm the hex in Figma. It is the kit's indigo, not a brand colour — flagged to design.

infoSoft.use: Tinted badge behind an info mark

warningSoft.use: Tinted badge behind a warning mark. The warning colour itself is Marigold (`accent`).

danger.use: Error sheet heading, mark and button ('That didn't go through', 'Email verification failed')
danger.note: Brighter than the brand error #A61B29, and the same in both schemes. Read off a screenshot; confirm the hex in Figma. A red button contradicts the usage rule 'never use Crimson for buttons' — flagged to design.

dangerSoft.use: Tinted badge behind an error mark

focusRing.use: Ring around the OTP box the next digit goes into

border.use: No dark border exists in the brief; derived one step above Deep so dividers stay visible. Confirm with design.

heading.note: The dark sign-up mockup keeps brand teal for headings. That is 3.0:1 on Night: enough for the 32pt headings (WCAG large text), weak for smaller ones. Flagged to design; Teal Light #2BB3A3 is the accessible alternative.

link.note: Marigold on Night, from the dark sign-up mockup.

track.note: The dark sign-up and password-reset frames keep the light track: inactive step segments, unmet rule marks and code-box outlines are the same pale grey as on white. Was a derived #34443F.

successSoft.note: The dark 'Email verified!' sheet keeps the light badge tint rather than a dark one (was #173A2B, derived before the dark sheet was drawn).

successTitle.note: Mist, not teal: the dark 'Email verified!' sheet sets its heading in the text colour.

info.note: No dark info sheet is drawn; kept as on light, as the dark error sheet keeps its red.

infoSoft.note: Light tint on dark, as the drawn dark success and error badges are.

warningSoft.note: Light tint on dark, as the drawn dark success and error badges are.

focusRing.note: Marigold on Night, from the dark Verification frame.

kitLeftovers.$note: Present in the Figma file but NOT part of the brand system. Recorded so they are recognised and rejected in review, not copied into code.

usageRules: Roughly 60% neutrals, 30% Teal, 10% Coral and Marigold. Coral loses its pull if it is everywhere.
One coral CTA per screen where possible.
Never use Coral for errors, and never use Crimson for buttons.

typography.licence: All three are Google Fonts under the SIL OFL. latin + latin-ext subsets shipped, for accented traveller and destination names.

labelXs.note: Figma has this as DM Sans 500 with kit grey #666D80. Normalised to Inter + brand secondary text. See docs/DESIGN_TOKENS.md.

layout.$note: Measured from the Properties panel on Onboarding Screen_Variant 2 (node 167-7636) and the Create Account screen (iPhone 14 & 15 Pro, 393pt).

button.$note: Measured on the Onboarding Next button (Figma Button component, Size=Large). Radius 80 on a 44pt button renders as a full pill — the tooltip on the Corner_Radius chip reads 80px.

input.$note: Measured on the Create Account screen. A field with a trailing icon is taller because the 20pt icon sets its height.

touchTarget.$note: The smallest tap area for an icon-only control: Apple's HIG asks for 44pt, Material for 48dp. The glyph keeps its drawn size; the target extends around it.

socialButton.$note: The 'Sign up with …' buttons are rounded rectangles, not pills.
